Subject: Re: Order Form draft — output & model use

Vanessa —

Thanks for sending the Order Form. Our legal team reviewed the current language and we have three non-negotiable items related to IP and model use:

1) Output ownership: Lumen requires an explicit clause confirming Customer owns the output (generated text/data) and Redwood only has a limited service right to display/produce those outputs for the Customer.
2) Training rights: We cannot grant rights for Redwood to use Customer inputs or outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve models unless we provide prior written consent.
3) Feedback: Any feedback Redwood asks for must not be used to create productized models for other customers; at most it can be used for debugging and aggregated telemetry.

Attached is our redline on the Order Form and a short memo from our counsel explaining potential regulatory concerns about using healthcare-related outputs for training. Please let us know where Redwood can be flexible (e.g., anonymized aggregate telemetry for service quality) and where you need to escalate.

Best,
Samir
Head of Contracts, Lumen Health
attachments: Lumen_OrderForm_markedup.docx, lumen_training_memo.pdf

Subject: Re: Order Form draft — output & model use

Samir / Marta —

Thanks for the redline and the memo — appreciate the clarity. We want to get this over the finish line quickly. High-level responses:

- Output ownership: We are comfortable acknowledging Customer ownership of outputs for their own use. We typically carve out a very narrow "service rights" grant so Redwood can reproduce responses in logs and debug issues; we propose the language below.
- Training rights: We cannot accept an absolute prohibition across all telemetry because we rely on aggregated, anonymized telemetry to maintain service quality and safety. However, we can remove any right to train our base models on Customer-provided data or outputs without express written consent. We can agree to a stronger "no training on PII/PHI" protection and to define telemetry categories we may use.
- Feedback: We can accept a limited feedback license that permits use for service improvement only, not for training generalized base models used by third parties.

I've attached our proposed snippet (RDWD_proposed_feedback_clause.txt) and a redline on your order form that flags the MSA sections that need cross-reference. If this looks ok, can Priya and Markus weigh in on the exact redlines? We also included a DocuSign link to keep momentum on the commercial terms once the legal language is agreed.

Proposed short language to discuss: "Customer retains ownership of Outputs. Provider may retain copies of Outputs only to the extent necessary to provide the Service, debug issues, and comply with law. Provider shall not use Customer Inputs or Outputs to train or improve Provider's base models without Customer's prior written consent; limited, aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry may be used to monitor and operate the Service. Feedback provided by Customer may be used by Provider solely to improve the Service but shall not be used to create derivative models for resale to third parties."

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: RDWD_proposed_feedback_clause.txt, Lumen_OrderForm_redline.docx

Vanessa / Markus —

Thanks for the context and the proposed language. Draft guidance and our recommended redline approach below — short version first: we can accept Customer ownership of Outputs and a strict prohibition on using Customer Inputs/Outputs to train base models, while permitting the Provider to use limited, aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry for safety/ops. We will also add a mechanism to request narrow, explicit consent for model training in writing (per-deal).

Suggested clause (short form for Order Form):
"Customer Data and Outputs. Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to the Outputs. Provider may retain copies of Outputs solely for the purpose of providing the Service, debugging, compliance, and as required by law. Provider shall not use Customer Data or Outputs to train, improve, or otherwise create or update Provider's base foundation models, or any model used outside the scope of this Order Form, without Customer's prior written consent. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Provider may collect and use aggregated, de-identified telemetry solely to monitor, maintain, and improve the performance and security of the Service ("Telemetry"), provided such Telemetry cannot reasonably be re-identified."

Feedback License (to be added to MSA):
"Feedback. Customer may provide feedback about the Service. Provider may use such feedback solely to operate, maintain and improve the Service provided to Customer and shall not use Customer Feedback to create or train generalized models for third party resale. Any use of Feedback for other purposes shall require Customer's prior written consent."

Redlines: we will produce an editable redline of the MSA and Order Form that inserts these clauses and cross-references Section 12 (Confidentiality) and Section 17 (Data Security). We should also propose definitions for "Outputs", "Customer Data", and "Telemetry" so the scope is clear.

Commercial note: if customer requires an absolute prohibition (including on Telemetry), Sales should present the trade-offs: higher per-call pricing and a narrower SLA (we will need to exclude certain safety monitoring that relies on telemetry). If Lumen is unwilling to provide a written opt-in for model training in the future, we recommend adding an annual review clause for any potential consent.

I'll attach the redline in the Drive link and prepare a short memo addressing PHI concerns (how telemetry filters and suppression work). Expect the redline within 3 hours.

Priya Natarajan
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
